lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.empty: Statement requires m,n>=1, so column vectorization has actual entries; an individual zero matrix is allowed but is not an absent coordinate family.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.zero: Proof step1.1 compares sums of squared absolute entries, giving zero on both sides for X=0; steps1.2–2.1 use only products and addition, not division by its norm.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.one: When m=n=1, proof steps1.1–2.1 reduce to the scalar absolute-value identity and AX+XB=(A+B)X; the same column-stack convention applies.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.degenerate: The Kronecker/vectorization identities require compatible finite shapes only, with no rank or invertibility hypothesis on A,B or X.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.endpoints: The column-stack identities have finite integer indices and no time, tolerance or spectral-limit endpoint.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.nonempty-choice: The column-stacking map and Kronecker blocks are explicit finite coordinate formulas; no basis or vector selection is left unspecified.
lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and.logic: The lemma proves two algebraic identities for the specified column convention, not an iff characterization of a general vectorization map.

lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.empty: Statement q>=1 excludes a zero-order input but explicitly declares the empty product when q=1, so its exponent q-1=0 is intentional.
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.zero: Proof step1.1 handles M=0 by delta=0=sigma_min; only the M!=0 branch in steps1.2–2.1 divides by ||M||_F^(q-1)>0.
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.one: For q=1 the denominator is its zeroth power1 on the nonzero branch; the stated empty-product convention gives delta(M)=|det M|=sigma_min(M).
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.degenerate: Proof step1.2 admits zero smallest singular value and hence singular nonzero M; its determinant product vanishes and the lower bound delta=0 remains valid.
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.endpoints: This determinant estimate is algebraic in a fixed finite matrix; there is no interval parameter, while the norm-zero boundary is handled explicitly before division.
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.nonempty-choice: One finite SVD supplies its finite singular-value list for this matrix; the proof asserts no simultaneous SVD selection over a matrix family.
lem-small-block-determinant-separation-l.logic: The small-block result supplies the inequality0<=delta<=sigma_min, not an equivalence between an arbitrary threshold rejection and singularity.

def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.empty: Definition n>=1 gives a positive-order matrix and a genuine complex spectrum; zero forcing Q or zero trial X are permitted and do not remove the coefficient's state space.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.zero: Definition allows Q=0 and X=0 in the Lyapunov equation, but the zero coefficient matrix is not Hurwitz because its eigenvalue0 has no strictly negative real part.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.one: Definition includes a scalar coefficient with negative real part and a scalar self-adjoint forcing; transpose versus adjoint conventions remain explicit.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.degenerate: Hurwitz means strict negativity of every complex eigenvalue; zero real spectral part is excluded, whereas semidefinite forcing is a separately defined allowed predicate.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.endpoints: The Hurwitz definition is a strict spectral predicate, not a closed time-interval assertion; eigenvalues on the imaginary axis are outside that predicate.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.nonempty-choice: This item imposes predicates on a given finite matrix and supplied self-adjoint forcing, with no choice of an eigenbasis or Lyapunov solution.
def-hurwitz-matrix-and-continuous-lyapun.logic: The item defines the Hurwitz spectral convention and Lyapunov equation; it does not prove a stability-versus-positive-solution equivalence.

lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.empty: Statement assumes q>=1; the q=1 cofactor uses the defined determinant of its zero-order minor, not an empty input matrix to the theorem.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.zero: Proof step3.1 takes adj(M)/det(M) only when det(M)!=0; the other branch invokes singularity instead of evaluating an inverse at determinant0.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.one: For q=1 the sole adjugate cofactor is1, and proof step2.1 reduces M*1=det(M)I_1, giving the scalar reciprocal exactly when the entry is nonzero.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.degenerate: Proof step2.1's off-diagonal cofactors use a repeated-row determinant0, and step3.1 keeps singular matrices in the det=0 branch rather than assuming all matrices invertible.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.endpoints: The adjugate identity concerns exact field arithmetic with no numerical tolerance or limiting time endpoint; determinant zero is the explicit algebraic case split.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.nonempty-choice: Every cofactor and the adjugate are given finite determinant formulas; no arbitrary solution vector or inverse candidate is selected.
lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-fiel.logic: The Statement gives the adjugate product identity and its nonzero/zero determinant consequences; it is not phrased as an algorithm-success iff criterion.

def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.empty: Definition m,n>=1 makes the Frobenius unit sphere nonempty; the finite SVD supplies an attained smallest singular value rather than a minimum over an empty set.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.zero: Definition permits sep(A,-B)=0 for a singular Sylvester operator; no reciprocal of the separation is taken in this definition itself.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.one: For m=n=1 the defined map is multiplication by A+B and its separation is |A+B| in the one-dimensional Frobenius norm.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.degenerate: The separation definition covers singular A or B and even a singular Sylvester map; later positive-separation estimates, not this item, exclude a zero minimum.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.endpoints: The operator/separation definition has no step-size or time interval; zero separation is a valid value of the defined minimum.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.nonempty-choice: The finite SVD guarantees the minimum for one finite-dimensional map; the item does not choose a minimizer for an infinite family of operators.
def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-nu.logic: This item defines X->AX+XB and its separation with the conventional label -B, without asserting a new biconditional solvability theorem.

lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.empty: The inherited Hurwitz convention has n>=1, so the truncated sum from k=0 to n-1 contains its k=0 term. For n=1 that sole term is1 and there is no nontrivial nilpotent factor.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.zero: Proof step3.1's ordered-integral construction admits N=0 as a strictly upper-triangular part; all positive-order terms vanish. Its factorial denominators are positive integers, including0!=1.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.one: At n=1, proof step4.1 leaves only the scalar exponential term e^(-alpha*t), matching a one-entry Hurwitz Schur form.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.degenerate: The bound does not require diagonalizable A; proof step3.1 retains strictly upper-triangular Schur factors and kills a remainder only after n such index increases.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.endpoints: Statement t>=0 includes t=0: proof step4.1's k=0 term is1 and all positive-degree simplex volumes vanish, giving ||I||_2=1.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.nonempty-choice: One finite Schur triangularization is supplied or obtained from the stated finite-dimensional theorem, and the finite ordered-integral expansion needs no choice of forms over time.
lem-hurwitz-matrix-exponential-decay-bou.logic: The Hurwitz lemma gives a sufficient exponential-polynomial upper bound; it does not characterize all matrices whose exponential happens to satisfy some decay estimate.

lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.empty: The coefficient is a positive-order Hurwitz matrix under its definition; proof step1.1's hypothetical nonzero kernel is a single finite-dimensional space, not an empty index family.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.zero: Statement Re(p)<0 excludes p=0 before the argument. Proof step1.1 never divides by p; singularity would give an eigenvalue -p with positive real part.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.one: For order1, the same argument says a scalar Hurwitz entry cannot equal -p in the open right half-plane, so its shifted scalar is nonzero.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.degenerate: Proof steps1.1–2.1 derive a contradiction from any hypothetical singular shifted matrix; no diagonalizability or real-only shift restriction is imposed.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.endpoints: The shift hypothesis is strict Re(p)<0. The imaginary-axis endpoint is outside this theorem and is not justified by taking a limit in its contradiction argument.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.nonempty-choice: The proof assumes one singular shifted matrix for contradiction and instantiates one nonzero kernel vector; it chooses no vector across all shifts.
lem-hurwitz-negative-shift-matrix-invert.logic: This negative-shift lemma is a sufficient invertibility implication under Hurwitz and left-half-plane shift assumptions, not a converse classification of invertible shifts.

lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.empty: The defined Sylvester operator has m,n>=1; its unit sphere in proof step1.1 is used only after a particular nonzero X has been normalized.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.zero: Proof step1.1 first discharges X=0 as equality and divides by ||X||_F only otherwise. Step2.1 divides by sep only under the Statement's strict positive-separation hypothesis.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.one: For a scalar Sylvester map the two proof steps give |X|<=|(A+B)X|/|A+B| under |A+B|>0, including equality and X=0.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.degenerate: Singular A and B separately are allowed if their Sylvester separation remains positive; the theorem excludes a singular Sylvester operator, not all individually singular coefficients.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.endpoints: There is no time endpoint in the Frobenius error inequality; sep=0 is explicitly outside its strict hypothesis and no zero-denominator extension is asserted.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.nonempty-choice: The normalized matrix is the explicit Y=X/||X||, so the estimate needs no arbitrary minimizing-vector choice.
lem-sylvester-separation-controls-the-fr.logic: The lemma proves a norm lower-bound consequence of positive separation, not an iff between a particular residual and invertibility.

thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.empty: Statement m,n>=1 supplies positive matrix orders. An empty spectral intersection is the actual solvability condition, not a missing input spectrum or an omitted empty case.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.zero: Proof steps1.2–2.1 require every eigenvalue sum t_ii+s_jj nonzero precisely for invertibility; a zero sum is retained as the failure of that condition.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.one: For scalar A,B the proof's Kronecker matrix has one entry A+B, so spectral disjointness is exactly A+B!=0 and the unique solution exists for every scalar right-hand side.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.degenerate: Proof step3.1 compares the same real Kronecker determinant over R and C, retaining real matrices with nonreal eigenvalues; repeated eigenvalues are allowed if no forbidden sum vanishes.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.endpoints: This exact spectral equivalence has no tolerance or time endpoint; the boundary sep=0 belongs to the noninvertible side of proof step4.1.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.nonempty-choice: The two finite Schur decompositions and the finite-dimensional SVD criterion supply this one operator's equivalences; there is no simultaneous choice of solutions for all right-hand sides in the proof.
thm-sylvester-unique-solvability-spectra.logic: Proof steps1.2–2.1 identify invertibility with all eigenvalue sums nonzero in both directions; step3.1 transfers this to real inputs and step4.1 equates bijectivity, unique solvability for every C and strictly positive separation.

thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.empty: The inherited Hurwitz convention has positive dimension and the integral runs on the nonempty half-line. Zero forcing is allowed but is not an absent integral domain.
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.zero: Proof steps2.1–3.1 allow Q=0 and produce X=0. Step3.2 then gives semidefiniteness, while strict positivity correctly fails for nonzero vectors remaining in ker(Q^(1/2)).
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.one: For a scalar Hurwitz coefficient the same improper integral and continuous nonnegative integrand proof apply; no two-dimensional observability assumption is introduced.
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.degenerate: Proof step3.2 proves X>=0 from semidefinite Q, and step5.1 uses the full trajectory-kernel condition before concluding strict positivity; rank-deficient forcing is not silently treated as positive definite.
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.endpoints: Proof step3.2 uses positivity of the integrand at t=0 and continuity on a positive-length interval, and step3.1 takes the justified decaying T->infinity limit.
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.nonempty-choice: The solution is defined entrywise by uniquely determined improper integrals and uniqueness follows from exponential decay, without choosing among Lyapunov solutions.
thm-continuous-lyapunov-integral-and-pos.logic: Proof step5.1 shows a nonnegative continuous integrand has zero integral exactly when it vanishes at every time, and this equals remaining in ker(Q^(1/2)); both directions give the stated strict-positivity criterion.

alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.empty: Definition explicitly initializes zero-column Z0, X0=0 and R0=B; a zero-length shift list performs no update and returns those initialized quantities as completed.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.zero: Definition rejects Re(p)>=0 before c=-2Re(p)>0 and checks the shifted system before inversion. Zero forcing B is admitted and makes all exact updates zero.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.one: One admissible real shift makes one update, while a lone nonreal shift with real data fails the explicit consecutive-conjugate pairing scan.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.degenerate: Definition consumes accepted nonreal pairs in validation but still updates both individual shifts; it keeps invalid/unpaired/singular statuses and asserts no real-factor or unconditional convergence consequence.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.endpoints: The finite shift list includes its last partner exactly once in the scan. A shift with real part0 is rejected, rather than normalized as though c>0.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.nonempty-choice: The shifts are supplied as a finite list and exact shifted solves are input operations; the procedure does not choose convergence-producing shifts.
alg-low-rank-alternating-direction-impli.logic: ADI here is a finite prescribed approximation procedure with explicit statuses, not an equivalence between completing its shift list and solving the Lyapunov equation exactly.

thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.empty: The operator domain inherited from its Definition has positive matrix orders; the error equation compares one exact solution with one supplied approximation.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.zero: Proof step1.1 gives S(E)=R and step2.1 divides only by the assumed positive separation; R=0 then forces E=0, including an exactly correct approximation.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.one: For a one-entry equation, proof step2.1 is the exact scalar inequality |X-Xhat|<=|R|/|A+B| with the nonzero coefficient guaranteed by separation.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.degenerate: The theorem does not infer a useful error bound from residual alone when separation vanishes; its Statement explicitly requires sep>0 before using the inverse scale.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.endpoints: The residual bound has no time or parameter interval; a small positive separation is retained and magnifies the residual, while sep0 is excluded.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.nonempty-choice: The exact solution is uniquely specified by the stated equation and positive separation, and the error E=X-Xhat is explicit rather than an arbitrary selection.
thm-sylvester-residual-to-forward-error-.logic: The residual theorem gives an upper forward-error implication under positive separation, not a converse guarantee that small error implies a particular residual certificate.

thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.empty: Proof step1.1 proves the completed-iterate base j=0 directly: X0=0 and R0=B give BB*=R0R0*, so the zero-update case is not skipped.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.zero: Proof step3.1 factors the residual as R_j R_j*, allowing a zero residual factor and exact solution without dividing by either residual or forcing norm.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.one: Proof steps1.2–3.1 establish one actual individual-shift update from the initialized factor, so a single real shift is included in the induction.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.degenerate: The identity is conditional on a completed update with its admitted exact shifted solve; it does not assign the recurrence to an invalid or failed shift.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.endpoints: Only the finite completed update index is involved; the base j0 and each later successful update have explicit identities, with no infinite-time convergence assertion.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.nonempty-choice: The actual completed ADI recurrence supplies V_j,X_j and R_j; the proof expands those fixed matrices rather than choosing an alternative residual factorization.
thm-low-rank-adi-exact-residual-factor-i.logic: The ADI result proves a residual-factor identity at each completed iterate, not an equivalence between a prescribed residual size and convergence of all shifts.

thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.empty: The rational product at j=0, if included, is the empty product I and gives R0=B, consistent with the initialized residual supplier. For j>=1 proof step1.1 multiplies the actual admitted shift factors; the bound is never based on an empty state space.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.zero: Proof step1.2 proves sep(A,-A*)>0 from Hurwitz spectral disjointness before division. Zero B or residual is allowed, while admissible negative-real shifts make each inverse A+pI defined.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.one: For a single admitted shift, proof step1.1 gives exactly its one rational factor times B; for a scalar matrix the Frobenius/SVD bound becomes the scalar absolute-value estimate.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.degenerate: The Statement retains the independent proved rational operator estimate ||rho_j(A)||<=eta_j with eta_j->0; a finite shift list or a merely completed run does not supply it.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.endpoints: Proof step3.1 takes j->infinity only under the supplied eta_j->0 bound and fixed positive separation; it does not extrapolate convergence from one finite residual certificate.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.nonempty-choice: The admissible shift sequence and proved rational norm bound are supplied hypotheses; this theorem does not choose a sequence achieving convergence.
thm-low-rank-adi-conditional-convergence.logic: The ADI convergence theorem is expressly conditional on the external rational shift estimate, not an iff between Hurwitz stability and success of arbitrary shifts.

alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.empty: Definition assumes m,n>=1 but its first column-increasing,row-decreasing local solve has empty prior-block sums, explicitly contributing zero to F_ij before any previous block is available.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.zero: Definition tests det(M_ij)=0 before using the adjugate quotient; even at tau=0 a singular pivot cannot enter a stored solve, and zero right-hand side remains permitted.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.one: Definition includes local one-by-one complex pivots and scalar input arrays; the same exact certificate/threshold checks apply without a two-block traversal.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.degenerate: Schur candidates remain unaccepted until exact factor identities pass; missing certificates or threshold rejections return declared failures rather than claiming an exact solution.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.endpoints: Finite sweep and controller budgets are nonnegative, and zero budget can return undecided/failure before substitution. No real-time endpoint or positive-budget success promise is made.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.nonempty-choice: The fixed sign program, actual finite traversal and adjugate formula determine accepted local solutions; arbitrary-terminating mode is an explicit input contract, not a choice of a terminating program.
alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation.logic: The Bartels-Stewart algorithm defines success after exact checks and local solves, not an iff equating algebraic solvability with its finite controller or threshold acceptance.

ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.empty: The covariance-balance witness fixes a two-by-two A and the one-column forcing B=(1,1); no absent noise factor or empty spectrum is substituted.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.zero: Verification step2.1 completes squares and permits the zero test vector, with strict positivity asserted only for nonzero(u,v); none of the rational entries divides by a variable that may vanish.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.one: The forcing has one column but its two-dimensional covariance is full positive definite, as verification step2.1 proves from the nonnegative square decomposition.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.degenerate: Example explicitly verifies the algebraic covariance balance only; it does not infer a separate stochastic realization or stationary-law theorem from that matrix identity.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.endpoints: The fixed covariance equation contains no time interval or numerical tolerance; its exact rational entries are checked at the supplied stable matrix.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.nonempty-choice: The matrix X is displayed and verified directly; uniqueness from the Hurwitz integral theorem removes any unspecified covariance selection.
ex-stable-linear-noise-lyapunov-covarian.logic: This example gives one exact positive Lyapunov balance solution, not a biconditional characterization of stationary stochastic models.

ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.empty: The sensitivity witness fixes two-by-two diagonal A,B and the matrix unit E11, so its four eigenvalue sums form a nonempty explicit list.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.zero: Verification step1.1 uses epsilon=10^-6>0 before step2.1 divides by it; a zero perturbation delta is allowed and yields zero solution change in step3.1.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.one: Verification step3.1 perturbs only the single E11 coordinate, attaining the separation amplification exactly rather than averaging over an eigenmode family.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.degenerate: The smallest sum epsilon is tiny but nonzero; all other sums remain nonzero, so the example illustrates large sensitivity without asserting singularity at its fixed input.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.endpoints: The Example fixes epsilon=10^-6 rather than including epsilon=0; no division or uniqueness claim at the exact spectral collision is asserted.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.nonempty-choice: All diagonal eigenvalue sums and the perturbed matrix-unit direction are explicit, so no worst-case direction selection is hidden in this sensitivity example.
ex-nearly-colliding-sylvester-eigenvalue.logic: The near-collision example computes a particular attained residual amplification, not an equivalence between every large forward error and its chosen matrix pair.

ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.empty: Example uses exactly one admitted real shift on a two-dimensional matrix with one forcing column; it is not a zero-update approximation disguised as a residual test.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.zero: Verification step2.1 obtains R1=0 by exact cancellation and step3.1 verifies the full Lyapunov residual0 directly, with no relative-residual division.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.one: The single shift p1=-1 makes one shifted solve and one rank-one factor update; verification step1.1 uses the invertible matrix -2I.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.degenerate: This witness's zero residual certifies its exact displayed Lyapunov solution, without adding an unconditional convergence claim for other finite shift lists.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.endpoints: No time interval or limit is involved: the example stops after its one exact ADI update and records the resulting residual factor.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.nonempty-choice: The shift, forcing vector, inverse and rank-one factors are all displayed, so the exact residual witness requires no shift-selection rule.
ex-low-rank-adi-residual-certificate.logic: The ADI example verifies one zero-residual factorization, not an iff between a finite shift count and exactness for every Lyapunov equation.
